rows.description: I break my biscuit and give half to a friend who has none. I feel proud and warm inside. Real sharing is chosen, not forced; a wise adult praises the kindness and does not demand I give away everything.
A friend shares their tiffin with me when mine is forgotten. I feel happy and a bit shy. I say thank you and plan to share back another day; grabbing more than was offered would spoil the kindness.
A classmate tops every test and I feel small and bitter. Wise: study their method and accept that ranks are one narrow measure. Harmful: spreading rumours or hiding notes.
Friends grow cold after I score well. Wise: stay warm, share notes, do not flaunt marks, and accept some distance may pass. Harmful: shrinking my effort to be liked.

I want closeness with my partner but they are tired or unsure. Real intimacy means asking, listening to a no without sulking, and understanding that willingness must be free; pressure or guilt-tripping is not love.

I am not in the mood or not ready and I fear disappointing my partner. My comfort matters equally; I can say no kindly and clearly, and a caring partner respects it. Repeated pressure is a warning sign to speak to someone trusted.
A coworker is treated unfairly, and you speak up or support them. Solidarity carries risk, so do it with facts and allies. Silence teaches everyone that injustice is normal.

A coworker stands by you when you are treated unfairly. Thank them, protect them from consequences where you can, and remember the debt. Such support often makes the difference between giving up and continuing.
They said no or did not feel the same. It stings badly. Wise: accept it without pressing, grieve with friends, and let it teach me. Harmful: pestering, spreading rumours, or calling them cruel.
Someone likes me and I do not feel the same. Wise: say a kind, clear no with no mixed signals, keep their dignity, and do not mock them. Harmful: leading them on for attention.

My partner and my parents are in conflict and I feel pulled apart. I stay loyal to my marriage while treating my parents with respect, refuse to carry tales between them, and do not make my partner the villain.

My partner keeps taking their parents' side against me and I feel alone in my own home. I say what I need, ask us to face the issue as a team, and hold dignity without demanding they cut ties with their family.
